name: Anton Long
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember copying an illustration ruined by hot chocolate.” Saturday often includes a stop at the corner by Juniper Tailor, where Anton looks at the things people actually bring in for repair before looking in the display window.
voice: I spilled coffee on page six and copied the page by hand. Thirty years later my hand looks like my mum's.
appearance: Anton has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for a loose dark braid. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Anton draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Anton has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To show the copied page to the original lender.
family: Zara Kang is Anton’s cousin raised in the same household. Anton sets the time to leave. Zara picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The ladder crossing*, Zara says, “My wife stepped between the rungs laughing.”
connections: Elaine Aguilar. They compare an exact replacement with the original damaged page.

reactions.response: Anton lets the book go back with the note folded inside.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Anton takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.
